arxiv-1706-01679.title: On the Feasibility of Distinguishing Between Process Disturbances and Intrusions in Process Control Systems using Multivariate Statistical Process Control
arxiv-1706-01679.creator: Mikel Iturbe 1 , José Camacho 2 , Iñaki Garitano 1 , Urko Zurutuza 1 , Roberto Uribeetxeberria 1
arxiv-1706-01679.description: Abstract Process Control Systems (PCSs) are the operating core of Critical Infrastructures (CIs). As such, anomaly detection has been an active research field to ensure CI normal operation. Previous approaches have leveraged network level data for anomaly detection, or have disregarded the existence of process disturbances, thus opening the possibility of mislabelling disturbances as attacks and vice versa.

arxiv-2106-03528.title: Squeezing the Axion
arxiv-2106-03528.creator: Jondalar L. J. Kuß a, David J. E. Marsh b
arxiv-2106-03528.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jondalar L. J. Kuß a, David J. E. Marsh b. We apply the squeezed state formalism to scalar field dark matter (e.g. axion) perturbations generated during inflation. As for the inflationary perturbations, the scalar field state becomes highly squeezed as modes exit the horizon.

arxiv-2301-01255.title: More insights into symmetries in multisymplectic field theories Thanks: aguerrgu54@alumnes.ub.edu ( ORCID : 0000-0001-8738-274X). Thanks: narciso.roman@upc.edu ( ORCID : 0000-0003-3663-9861).
arxiv-2301-01255.creator: [1ex] Departament de Física Quàntica i Astrofísica, Universitat de Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain, [1ex] Department of Mathematics, Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, Barcelona, Spain
arxiv-2301-01255.description: Abstract This work provides a general overview for the treatment of symmetries in classical field theories and (pre)multisymplectic geometry. The geometric characteristics of the relation between how symmetries are interpreted in theoretical physics and in the geometric formulation of these theories are clarified.

arxiv-2305-16440.title: Representation Transfer Learning via Multiple Pre-trained models for Linear Regression
arxiv-2305-16440.creator: Navjot Singh, Suhas Diggavi
arxiv-2305-16440.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the problem of learning a linear regression model on a data domain of interest (target) given few samples. To aid learning, we are provided with a set of pre-trained regression models that are trained on potentially different data domains (sources).

arxiv-2307-02278.title: Smooth Particle Mesh Ewald-integrated stochastic Lanczos Many-body Dispersion algorithm
arxiv-2307-02278.creator: Pier Paolo Poier ∗, Louis Lagardère, Jean-Philip Piquemal ∗
arxiv-2307-02278.description: Abstract We derive and implement an alternative formulation of the Stochastic Lanczos algorithm to be employed in connection with the Many-Body Dispersion model (MBD). Indeed, this formulation, which is only possible due to the Stochastic Lanczos’ reliance on matrix-vector products, introduces generalized dipoles and fields.

arxiv-2411-04289.title: Fast particle trajectories and integrability in quasiaxisymmetric and quasihelical stellarators
arxiv-2411-04289.creator: Amelia Chambliss \aff 1 \corresp, E. Paul \aff 1, S. R. Hudson \aff 2
arxiv-2411-04289.description: Abstract Even if the magnetic field in a stellarator is integrable, phase-space integrability for energetic particle guiding center trajectories is not guaranteed. Both trapped and passing particle trajectories can experience convective losses, caused by wide phase-space island formation, and diffusive losses, caused by phase-space island overlap.

arxiv-2506-11512.title: Prioritizing Alignment Paradigms over Task-Specific Model Customization in Time-Series LLMs
arxiv-2506-11512.creator: Wei Li 1 , Yunyao Cheng 2 , Xinli Hao 1 , Chaohong Ma 1 , Yuxuan Liang 3 , Bin Yang 4 , Christian S. Jensen 2 , Xiaofeng Meng 1 1 Renmin University of China, 2 Aalborg University, 3 Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou), 4 East China Normal University {leeway,xinli_hao,chaohma,x
arxiv-2506-11512.description: Abstract Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled unprecedented capabilities for time-series reasoning in diverse real-world applications, including medical, financial, and spatio-temporal domains. However, existing approaches typically focus on task-specific model customization, such as forecasting and anomaly detection, while overlooking the data itself, referred to as time-series primitives , which are essential for in-depth reasoning.

arxiv-2508-12461.description: Abstract In August 2025, OpenAI released GPT-OSS models, its first open weight large language models since GPT-2 in 2019, comprising two mixture of experts architectures with 120B and 20B parameters. We evaluated both variants against six contemporary open source large language models ranging from 14.

arxiv-2509-24735.title: Resolution of the Borel–Kolmogorov Paradox via the Maximum Entropy Principle
arxiv-2509-24735.creator: Raphaël Trésor Mykola Lukashchuk
arxiv-2509-24735.description: Abstract This paper presents a rigorous resolution of the Borel–Kolmogorov paradox using the Maximum Entropy Principle. We construct a metric-based framework for Bayesian inference that uniquely extends conditional probability to events of null measure. The results unify classical Bayes’ rules and provide a robust foundation for Bayesian inference in metric spaces.

arxiv-2512-04218.title: Time of appearance of a large gap in a dynamic Poisson point process
arxiv-2512-04218.description: Abstract We study the distribution of the ‘gap time’, the first time that a large gap appears, in the spatial birth and death point process on [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] in which particles are added uniformly in space at rate λ \lambda and are removed independently at rate 1 1 , as a function of the parameter λ

pmc-10591040.title: Shared GABA transmission pathology in dopamine agonist- and antagonist-induced dyskinesia
pmc-10591040.creator: Yoshifumi Abe, Sho Yagishita, Hiromi Sano, Yuki Sugiura, Masanori Dantsuji, Toru Suzuki, Ayako Mochizuki, Daisuke Yoshimaru, Junichi Hata, Mami Matsumoto, Shu Taira, Hiroyoshi Takeuchi, Hideyuki Okano, Nobuhiko Ohno, Makoto Suematsu, Tomio Inoue, Atsushi Nambu, Masahiko Watanabe, Kenji F. Tanaka
pmc-10591040.description: SummaryDyskinesia is involuntary movement caused by long-term medication with dopamine-related agents: the dopamine agonist 3,4-dihydroxy-L-phenylalanine (L-DOPA) to treat Parkinson’s disease (L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia [LID]) or dopamine antagonists to treat schizophrenia (tardive dyskinesia [TD]). However, it remains unknown why distinct types of medications for distinct neuropsychiatric disorders induce similar involuntary movements.

pmc-10738528.title: AGING AND THE LIVED EXPERIENCES OF TRANSGENDER AND GENDER NONCONFORMING OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10738528.creator: Jeanne Koller, Paul Urbanski
pmc-10738528.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Adults identifying as transgender and gender non-conforming (T/GNC) in the United States may experience adversity, victimization, and discrimination across the life span (McDowell, et al., 2019). T/GNC older adults have higher rates of poverty, homelessness, social isolation, depression, and violence compared to older adults in the general population and compared with lesbian, gay, and bisexual (LGB) older adults (Sloan & Benson, 2022). This descriptive phenomenological study utilized a purposive and snowball sampling strategy and sought to increase understanding of this diverse group.

pmc-11343826.title: Sequential therapy for hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer-associated renal cell carcinoma: a case report and report of a new family pedigree
pmc-11343826.creator: Ichiro Tsuboi, Momoko Araki, Shuhei Yokoyama, Gen Tanaka, Kazutaka Mitani, Saori Yosioka, Yusuke Kobayashi, Hirochika Nakajima, Taichi Nagami, Kohei Ogawa, Chiaki Koike, Koichiro Wada
pmc-11343826.description: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC) is a rare autosomal-dominant disorder caused by a heterozygous germline mutation in the fumarate hydratase (FH) gene. HLRCC is clinically characterized by the development of three tumors: uterine leiomyomata, cutaneous leiomyomata, and renal cell carcinoma (RCC). HLRCC-associated RCC is aggressive and diagnosed at a much earlier age than sporadic RCC.

pmc-12504798.title: Hemopneumothorax After Carotid Endarterectomy
pmc-12504798.creator: Simona Formánková, Michael Rousek, Jiří Pudil, Radek Pohnán
pmc-12504798.description: Spontaneous hemopneumothorax (SHP) is a rare condition characterized by the accumulation of air and blood in the pleural cavity without prior trauma. We present a case of a patient who underwent carotid endarterectomy for carotid artery stenosis. Two days postoperatively, she developed sudden respiratory distress, hypotension, tachycardia, and a decrease in hemoglobin levels.

pmc-12690769.title: PDNO-22 Case series on the management protocol of pineoblastoma and medulloblastoma at Parirenyatwa Group of Hospitals, Harare, Zimbabwe.
pmc-12690769.creator: Tafadzwa Moreen Dube, Simbarashe Sanyamandwe, Maximillian Dzowa, Shungu Ushewokunze, Luxwell Jokonya, Kazadi K Kalangu
pmc-12690769.description: ObjectivesTo investigate the management protocol for pineoblastoma and medulloblastoma tumors at Parirenyatwa Hospital.MethodsThe clinical and surgical records of 4 pediatric patients diagnosed with pineoblastoma and medulloblastoma managed at Parirenyatwa hospital between November 2024 and April 2025 were accessed from the archives and analysed.

pmc-12730737.title: Development and validation of a risk prediction model for chronic kidney disease among adult hypertensive patients having follow-up at University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialised Hospital, Ethiopia: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-12730737.creator: Ambaye Dejen Tilahun, Miteku Andualem Limenih, Atalay Goshu Muluneh, Workagegnehu Hailu, Degefaye Zelalem Anlay, Bikis Liyew, Achenef Asmamaw Muche
pmc-12730737.description: ObjectiveChronic kidney disease (CKD) arises due to uncontrolled hypertension (HTN). HTN significantly increases the risk of complications in vital organs, mainly the kidneys. If hypertensive individuals receive early intervention, the majority of these complications and deaths from CKD can be avoided.

pmc-12735451.title: Opuntia dillenii as a Nutraceutical and Dietary Resource for Disease Prevention and Management: A Systematic Review
pmc-12735451.creator: Nisa Buset-Ríos, Mussa Makran, Ruymán Santana-Farré, Elizabeth Johnson
pmc-12735451.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Chronic diseases are leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide and their prevalence is increasing due to aging and lifestyle factors. A central element in their pathophysiology is chronic low-grade inflammation, linking metabolic, cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, and proliferative disorders. In this context, Opuntia dillenii, a cactus species traditionally used in folk medicine, has attracted considerable scientific interest due to its promising nutraceutical potential.

pmc-12749724.title: Navigating the new normal: understanding the impact of COVID-19 on e-learning readiness among nursing students in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12749724.creator: Fatchima Laouali Moussa, Mahaman Laouali Moussa, Ali Kerari, Tagwa Omer, Thamer Abdullah Alsufayan, Musaad Bedah Alsahly, Aboubacar Laouali Moussa, Hussain Ahmed Sufyani, Najla Burayk Alharbi, Huda Saeed Binzager, Bander Hammad Alblowi, Fayez Bakhat Alawfi, Sally Hammad Alblowi, Zaheen Ahmed Iqbal
pmc-12749724.description: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated a sudden transition to e-learning, creating challenges for nursing education, which relies heavily on clinical and practical training. This study examined male nursing students’ fear of COVID-19, their e-learning readiness, and the relationship between these variables in Saudi Arabia. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 110 male nursing students from multiple Saudi universities.

pmc-13254643.title: Peripheral vascular rim on endoscopic ultrasound as a practical rule-in sign for pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms
pmc-13254643.creator: Eunae Cho
pmc-13254643.description: accounting for approximately 90% of cases. Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (pNENs) are the second most common, accounting for approximately 1% to 5%.2 Because prognosis, biology, and treatment strategies differ substantially among pancreatic tumors, rapidly differentiating PDAC from other tumors, particularly pNEN, is essential whenever a pancreatic mass is identified.

pmc-13440217.title: C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio and the mortality of patients with heart failure: a meta-analysis
pmc-13440217.creator: Yan Wang, Zhenfei Yuan
pmc-13440217.description: BackgroundThe C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) reflects the interplay between systemic inflammation and nutritional status, and has recently been proposed as a prognostic biomarker in heart failure (HF). However, its association with mortality risk across acute decompensated HF (ADHF) and chronic HF (CHF) populations remains uncertain. This meta-analysis evaluated the relationship between baseline CAR and all-cause mortality in HF.

pmc-13460912.title: Equity and Respect in Maternal and Infant Healthcare—A Report From the 2025 Venice Forum
pmc-13460912.creator: Mark Hanson, Ariadne Malamitsi‐Puchner, Flavia Bustreo, Gian Carlo Di Renzo, Hema Divaker, Joseph Haddad, Rajat Khosla, Anne Kihara, Donna Ockenden, Sandra Oyarzo‐Torres, Camilla Pickles, Lesley Regan, Jennifer Harris Requejo, Agnès Soucat, Kate Womersley, Neena Modi
pmc-13460912.description: AimTo examine equity and respectful care for women and infants from five perspectives: the global context; economic issues; healthcare systems; legal and policy issues; opportunities to benefit from biomedical research.MethodsNarrative review.ResultsHealthcare accounts for half the variance in health in low‐income countries and substantially less in high‐income settings; however, healthcare investment remains efficient and equitable.

pmc-13480389.title: Antibacterial Immunotherapy: Mechanistic Insights, Emerging Therapeutic Strategies, and Clinical Translation
pmc-13480389.creator: Hamdi Al-Azzani, Hanane Aliouat, Hongshi Cheng, Omer M A Dagah, Musaed Hamood Al-subari, Wenhu Zhou, Shugen Wu
pmc-13480389.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) continues to compromise the effectiveness of conventional antibacterial therapy, driving the development of therapeutic strategies that extend beyond direct antibiotic-mediated bacterial killing. Multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens evade treatment through diverse mechanisms, including enzymatic drug inactivation, target modification, efflux pump overexpression, biofilm formation, and persisters development.

pmc-13579751.title: The gut microbiome in the Lebanese population and its alterations in metastatic colorectal cancer: benchmarking and application
pmc-13579751.creator: Sally Temraz, Farah J Nassar, Pierre Bertrand, Razan Al Tartir, Maria Mezher, Ruba Hadla, Zahraa S Msheik, Ghada Chamandi, Vincent Cahais, Cyrille Cuenin, Ayman Al Shoukari, Ali Shamseddine, Hibeh Shatila, Farah Naja, Yinan Zheng, Lifang Hou, Rihab Nasr, Akram Ghantous
pmc-13579751.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) is a rising health concern in Lebanon and across the Arab world, concomitant with dietary and lifestyle transitions. The gut microbiome may contribute to CRC progression and treatment response, and it remains understudied in Arab populations.

pmc-13584210.title: Perceptions, knowledge and adoption of artificial intelligence in rheumatology: results from a British Society for Rheumatology survey
pmc-13584210.creator: Hansel Canagarajah, Pratyasha Saha, Jordan Tsigarides, Nicholas Fuggle, Meghna Jani
pmc-13584210.description: ObjectivesArtificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning applications are rapidly expanding across healthcare. Successful implementation of AI technologies in rheumatology will depend not only on technical performance but also on the perceptions and preparedness of end-users. This study evaluated the current opinions, expectations and concerns about AI among healthcare professionals and researchers in rheumatology across the UK.
